chapter: Orleans Pleasure Club to PWA band
title: Pianist Bunnell's remarkable ear
summary: Praises his pianist Bunnell, who could imitate Earl Hines, Duke Ellington and others, and recalls practicing at Peterson's place on Claiborne Street.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yes, indeed. He was the baddest piano player they had in the city in the Orleans. He was one of the best and couldn't really know. Fingers like Liv Rache. He could play just like Liv Rache in my book. You know what I mean? I'd say, just Albert and him play, I said, yeah I'm going to take me a little while Jack. Because I could never catch up with him. You know what I mean? His fingers was too fast. You understand? Because he'd play high society. Well he'd start to play in it. Then I'd say, all right, imitate Earl Hines. He'd imitate Earl Hines. I'd say, now, imitate Duke Ellington. He'd imitate Duke Ellington. I'd say, imitate Wayne King. He'd imitate Wayne King. You know any piano player that you could name, that he could play, he could imitate him. And see like sophisticated lady, all them car numbers, man he could play them numbers down. And nobody showed it to him. I don't know how he got them. I'm telling you. He had a wonderful ear. Oh he had this. And even, I know you know this guy too, his name is, he's got the music shop on there. He's got the music shop on Broad Street. Peter.
Peterson, yeah Peterson. Now we had a piano in Peterson's place on Claiborne Street when he had the piano. We used to go down and practice all the time.
Oh right in Peterson's place. Well where was the place on Claiborne Street?
On Claiborne between St. Peter and Lafitte.
Yeah, I never knew it then.
And he says, man I just wish I could have took them numbers down that he played. You know, record them. Well in them days I don't think they had a recording outfit. No, not like this.

He couldn't get no, he couldn't have no recording outfit to pick up on them numbers. Yeah. And that's how we used to do too, you know what I mean? And he said, no I was talking to them there today and he said, man I wish I could have recorded them numbers. He said they weren't money. Let's see who else.
